sanskrit: ṣoḍaśastrīsahasrāṇi vāsudevaparigrahaḥ nyamajjanta sarasvatyāṃ kālena janamejaya tāś cāpy apsaraso bhūtvā vāsudevam upāgaman
english: The sixteen thousand women who were the consorts of Vāsudeva, O Janamejaya, in time plunged into the Sarasvatī; and they too, becoming apsarases, went to Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: hatās tasmin mahāyuddhe ye vīrās tu mahārathāḥ ghaṭotkacādayaḥ sarve devān yakṣāṃś ca bhejire
english: Those heroic mighty warriors who were slain in that great battle—Ghaṭotkaca and all the rest—attained the company of the gods and the yakṣas.

sanskrit: duryodhanasahāyāś ca rākṣasāḥ parikīrtitāḥ prāptās te kramaśo rājan sarvalokān anuttamān
english: And the rākṣasas who are celebrated as the allies of Duryodhana, O king, in due order attained the most excellent of all the worlds.

sanskrit: bhavanaṃ ca mahendrasya kuberasya ca dhīmataḥ varuṇasya tathā lokān viviśuḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Those bulls among men entered the abode of great Indra, and of wise Kubera, and likewise the worlds of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ vistareṇa mahādyute kurūṇāṃ caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: All this has been recounted to you in full detail, O greatly radiant one—the entire history of the Kurus and of the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etac chrutvā dvijaśreṣṭhāt sa rājā janamejayaḥ vismito 'bhavad atyarthaṃ yajñakarmāntareṣv atha
english: The Sūta said: Having heard this from the foremost of the twice-born, that king Janamejaya was struck with the utmost wonder there in the intervals of the rites of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tataḥ samāpayām āsuḥ karma tat tasya yājakāḥ āstīkaś cābhavat prītaḥ parimokṣya bhujaṃgamān
english: Then his officiating priests brought that rite to completion, and Āstīka was well pleased, having delivered the serpents.

sanskrit: tato dvijātīn sarvāṃs tān dakṣiṇābhir atoṣayat pūjitāś cāpi te rājñā tato jagmur yathāgatam
english: Then he gratified all those twice-born ones with sacrificial fees; and, honored by the king, they departed as they had come.

sanskrit: visarjayitvā viprāṃs tān rājāpi janamejayaḥ tatas takṣaśilāyāḥ sa punar āyād gajāhvayam
english: And king Janamejaya too, having dismissed those brāhmaṇas, then returned once more from Takṣaśilā to the city named for the elephant.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ vaiśaṃpāyanakīrtitam vyāsājñayā samākhyātaṃ sarpasatre nṛpasya ha
english: All this, proclaimed by Vaiśaṃpāyana, has been recounted to you—told by the command of Vyāsa at the snake sacrifice of the king.

sanskrit: puṇyo 'yam itihāsākhyaḥ pavitraṃ cedam uttamam kṛṣṇena muninā vipra niyataṃ satyavādinā
english: Holy is this work called a history, and supremely purifying, O brāhmaṇa—composed by the sage Kṛṣṇa, the disciplined, the speaker of truth,

sanskrit: sarvajñena vidhijñena dharmajñānavatā satā atīndriyeṇa śucinā tapasā bhāvitātmanā
english: by the all-knowing, the knower of ordinance, the possessor of knowledge of dharma, the good, the transcender of the senses, the pure, whose soul was perfected by austerity,

sanskrit: aiśvarye vartatā caiva sāṃkhyayogavidā tathā naikatantravibuddhena dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā
english: who dwelt in sovereign power, who knew Sāṃkhya and Yoga, awakened in many systems of teaching, having beheld it with the divine eye,

sanskrit: kīrtiṃ prathayatā loke pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām anyeṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca bhūridraviṇatejasām
english: spreading abroad in the world the fame of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas and of other kṣatriyas abounding in wealth and splendor.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ śrāvayed vidvān sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi dhūtapāpmā jitasvargo brahmabhūyāya gacchati
english: The learned man who has this recited at every sacred season, his sins shaken off and heaven won, goes on to become one with Brahman.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ śrāvayec chrāddhe brāhmaṇān pādam antataḥ akṣayyam annapānaṃ vai pitṝṃs tasyopatiṣṭhate
english: And whoever has even a quarter of this recited to brāhmaṇas at a śrāddha, for him imperishable food and drink await his ancestors.

sanskrit: ahnā yad enaḥ kurute indriyair manasāpi vā mahābhāratam ākhyāya paścāt saṃdhyāṃ pramucyate
english: Whatever sin one commits by day, whether through the senses or even through the mind, by reciting the Mahābhārata one is afterward freed of it at the twilight prayer.

sanskrit: dharme cārthe ca kāme ca mokṣe ca bharatarṣabha yad ihāsti tad anyatra yan nehāsti na tat kva cit
english: In dharma, in artha, in kāma, and in mokṣa, O bull of the Bharatas—whatever is here may be found elsewhere; but what is not here is found nowhere at all.

sanskrit: jayo nāmetihāso 'yaṃ śrotavyo bhūtim icchatā rājñā rājasutaiś cāpi garbhiṇyā caiva yoṣitā
english: This history is named Jaya, the Victory, and should be heard by one who desires prosperity—by a king, by princes, and even by a woman with child.

sanskrit: svargakāmo labhet svargaṃ jayakāmo labhej jayam garbhiṇī labhate putraṃ kanyāṃ vā bahubhāginīm
english: He who longs for heaven may gain heaven; he who longs for victory may gain victory; the woman with child obtains a son, or a daughter of great fortune.

sanskrit: anāgataṃ tribhir varṣaiḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ saṃdarbhaṃ bhāratasyāsya kṛtavān dharmakāmyayā
english: The mighty Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, foreseeing things to come, in three years wrought the composition of this Bhārata out of love for dharma.

sanskrit: nārado 'śrāvayad devān asito devalaḥ pitṝn rakṣo yakṣāñ śuko martyān vaiśaṃpāyana eva tu
english: Nārada recited it to the gods, Asita Devala to the ancestors, Śuka to the rākṣasas and yakṣas, and Vaiśaṃpāyana indeed to mortals.

sanskrit: itihāsam imaṃ puṇyaṃ mahārthaṃ vedasaṃmitam śrāvayed yas tu varṇāṃs trīn kṛtvā brāhmaṇam agrataḥ
english: This holy history, of great import, equal to the Vedas—whoever recites it to the three varṇas, placing a brāhmaṇa at their head,

sanskrit: sa naraḥ pāpanirmuktaḥ kīrtiṃ prāpyeha śaunaka gacchet paramikāṃ siddhim atra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: that man, freed from sin and gaining renown here, O Śaunaka, will attain the supreme perfection—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: bhāratādhyayanāt puṇyād api pādam adhīyataḥ śraddadhānasya pūyante sarvapāpāny aśeṣataḥ
english: By the meritorious study of the Bhārata—even of one who studies but a quarter of it with faith—all sins are wholly purged away.

sanskrit: maharṣir bhagavān vyāsaḥ kṛtvemāṃ saṃhitāṃ purā ślokaiś caturbhir bhagavān putram adhyāpayac chukam
english: The great sage, the venerable Vyāsa, having of old composed this collection, in four verses the venerable one instructed his son Śuka.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛsahasrāṇi putradāraśatāni ca saṃsāreṣv anubhūtāni yānti yāsyanti cāpare
english: Thousands of mothers and fathers, and hundreds of sons and wives, experienced in the round of births, have passed away, and others yet will pass.

sanskrit: harṣasthānasahasrāṇi bhayasthānaśatāni ca divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam
english: Thousands of occasions for joy and hundreds for fear, day after day, beset the fool, but not the wise.

sanskrit: ūrdhvabāhur viraumy eṣa na ca kaś cic chṛṇoti me dharmād arthaś ca kāmaś ca sa kimarthaṃ na sevyate
english: With arms upraised I cry aloud, yet no one hears me: from dharma flow both artha and kāma—why then is dharma not pursued?

sanskrit: na jātu kāmān na bhayān na lobhād; dharmaṃ tyajej jīvitasyāpi hetoḥ nityo dharmaḥ sukhaduḥkhe tv anitye; jīvo nityo hetur asya tv anityaḥ
english: Never out of desire, nor out of fear, nor out of greed should one forsake dharma, even for the sake of life itself. Dharma is eternal, while pleasure and pain are fleeting; the soul is eternal, but its cause is transient.

sanskrit: imāṃ bhāratasāvitrīṃ prātar utthāya yaḥ paṭhet sa bhārataphalaṃ prāpya paraṃ brahmādhigacchati
english: He who, rising at dawn, recites this Sāvitrī of the Bhārata, gaining the fruit of the Bhārata attains the supreme Brahman.

sanskrit: yathā samudro bhagavān yathā ca himavān giriḥ khyātāv ubhau ratnanidhī tathā bhāratam ucyate
english: As the lordly ocean and as the Himālaya mountain are both renowned as treasuries of jewels, so is the Bhārata declared to be.

sanskrit: mahābhāratam ākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhet susamāhitaḥ sa gacchet paramāṃ siddhim iti me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: Whoever, well-composed in mind, recites the tale of the Mahābhārata will attain the supreme perfection—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: dvaipāyanoṣṭhapuṭaniḥsṛtam aprameyaṃ; puṇyaṃ pavitram atha pāpaharaṃ śivaṃ ca yo bhārataṃ samadhigacchati vācyamānaṃ; kiṃ tasya puṣkarajalair abhiṣecanena
english: For one who attains the Bhārata as it is recited—immeasurable, holy, purifying, sin-removing, and auspicious, sprung from the cradle of Dvaipāyana's lips—what need has he of consecration with the waters of the lotus-pool?
